Cc: procurement@coremed.com, legal@coremed.com
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on purge cadence options and proof of deletion for PHI

Vanessa — thanks for the call earlier. We need to fold a couple of specifics into the order form so our InfoSec and Legal teams can sign off: 

1) Can Redwood commit to a 30/90 hybrid purge model where: 
   - Non-PHI request data: purged from hot storage within 30 days and from backups within 90 days;
   - PHI flagged data: removed from serving nodes within 24 hours of request and certifiable deletion from backups within 180 days.

2) What evidence do you provide for deletion? We need an auditable deletion certificate and a log of the deletion job (job id + timestamp).

3) If CoreMed requires accelerated exit (e.g., contract termination), can you support a compressed timeline (30 days for all copies) as an add-on and what are the cost/levers?

Attaching our internal retention policy excerpt. Can you confirm if the above can be expressed in an Order Form appendix (bespoke windows) and what the standard exceptions are (encryption/QC holds)?

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Li
Senior Security Engineer, CoreMed Analytics
security@coremed.com

Jordan — really appreciate the clear ask and attaching the policy. Short answers up front: yes, we can represent bespoke windows in the Order Form appendix; we can provide an auditable deletion certificate and logs; compressed exit timelines are possible as a billable add-on with operational runbook.

High-level mapping to your bullets: 
- Non-PHI: 30-day hot purge / 90-day backup purge — standard configurable option.
- PHI: we can commit to removal from serving nodes within 24 hours of a deletion request. Backups are the tricky piece — we can certify backup-level deletion within 180 days under the standard Order Form appendix.
- Accelerated exit (30 days for all copies): supported via an "Accelerated Eviction" service — requires pre-approve scheduling window, runbook fees, and verification window; estimate added one-time fee (TBD).

I've attached a draft appendix that maps these terms into Order Form clauses (CoreMed_Custom_Purge_SLA_draft_v2.pdf) and a residency matrix for our environments. Ben / Marissa / Karthik — can you review the draft appendix for legal/commercial language and confirm the fee model for accelerated eviction? 

Jordan — I'll follow up with a proposed wording we can put straight into the order form (and include the deletion certificate template).

—Vanessa Ortiz

Draft for SOW clause below (tracked for legal review). Please review copy and flag anything that looks like an operational impossibility: 

"Deletion Certification and Audit Evidence" — Upon a validated data deletion request for customer-designated PHI, Redwood Inference will: 
1) Execute data removal from all serving and cache layers within 24 hours and log the deletion job (job id, initiating principal).
2) Initiate backup removal workflow; Redwood will provide an auditable Deletion Certificate within the agreed certification window (up to 180 days for PHI by default). The Deletion Certificate will include: 
   - Certificate ID and date/time of issuance;
   - Reference to the deletion job ID(s) and job timestamps;
   - Counts of objects targeted (aggregated, not raw IDs) and a hashed fingerprint of the deletion log file;
   - Statement of the deletion window (e.g., "Backups expected removed within 180 days from request date").
3) For Accelerated Eviction requests, Redwood will provide a compressed timeline and an Accelerated Deletion Certificate once runbook jobs complete. Accelerated Eviction is executed only after mutual scheduling approval and payment of the agreed fee.

Operational note: we should make clear that snapshots retained for regulatory holds may extend timelines; those will be listed as exceptions in the appendix.

Marissa Cole
Principal Product Counsel, Redwood Inference
